steps.tx: **Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis**, or **ARAS**, causes **90%** of **renovascular hypertension** cases, characteristically involving the aortic **ostium** and proximal third of the main renal artery in older patients with systemic vascular disease. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Fibromuscular dysplasia**, or **FMD**, causes **10%** of cases, predominantly affecting women aged **15** to **50** years. The classic **medial fibroplasia** subtype displays the pathognomonic **string-of-beads** appearance involving the mid and distal renal artery. Bilateral stenosis risks an acute fall in GFR when an ACE inhibitor removes efferent arteriolar tone.

steps.tx: The randomized **ASTRAL** and **CORAL** trials established that routine **renal artery stenting** added to comprehensive **medical therapy** confers no significant benefit in blood pressure control, preservation of kidney function, or cardiovascular outcomes in atherosclerotic disease. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Definitive clinical indications for renal **revascularization** in atherosclerotic disease include recurrent unexplained **flash pulmonary edema**, termed **Pickering syndrome**, refractory hypertension resistant to **4** anti-hypertensive classes, or acute decline during ACE inhibitor therapy. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: Bilateral high-grade RAS causing sudden volume surge
Class I indication for urgent stenting
Rapid progressive eGFR decline during ACEi therapy
Indicated to preserve remaining viable renal mass

steps.tx: Percutaneous transluminal **angioplasty**, or **PTRA**, performed without primary stenting, represents the gold standard therapy for **fibromuscular dysplasia**, achieving technical cure or substantial blood pressure improvement in up to **80%** of patients. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: FMD Revascularization
points: Procedure: Balloon angioplasty (PTRA) alone without stent
Target population: Young hypertensive women with medial fibroplasia
Cure rate: Complete cure of hypertension in up to 80%
Restenosis risk: Low long-term restenosis frequency

right.title: Atherosclerotic RAS Revascularization
points: Procedure: Balloon angioplasty with primary balloon-expandable stent
Target population: Older patients with refractory Pickering syndrome
Cure rate: Modest blood pressure reduction; rarely curative
Restenosis risk: Higher restenosis requiring surveillance

steps.tx: Doppler renal ultrasound diagnostic criteria for hemodynamically significant stenosis exceeding **60%** include a main renal artery **peak systolic velocity**, or **PSV**, exceeding **180** to **200** cm/s, and a **renal-to-aortic velocity ratio**, or **RAR**, greater than **3.5**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Atheroembolic renal disease**, or cholesterol crystal embolization, occurs after vascular catheterization, presenting with stepwise declining GFR, **livedo reticularis**, **blue toes**, hypocomplementemia, peripheral eosinophilia, and biconvex needle-shaped **cholesterol clefts** on renal biopsy. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Acute bilateral **renal artery occlusion** or acute occlusion in a solitary functioning kidney causes sudden **anuria**, severe unremitting flank pain, abrupt refractory hypertension, and markedly elevated serum **lactate dehydrogenase** levels reflecting extensive ischemic renal infarction. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Unilateral Stenosis
points: ACEi effect: Excretes excess sodium and controls hypertension
Total GFR: Stable total filtration maintained by healthy kidney

right.title: Bilateral Stenosis / Solitary Kidney
points: Renal perfusion: Bilaterally dependent on efferent constriction
ACEi effect: Efferent dilation collapses transcapillary pressure
Total GFR: Precipitous drop in GFR exceeding 30%
Therapy: Absolute contraindication to RAAS blockade
